Folks — preliminary triage below (runtime perspective):

What we see:
- The v2.4 rollout included an int8 conversion pass for certain model shards (q-profile: int8-legacy). On decode-heavy flows (short prompts + high concurrency) we're observing increased per-token decode time in the new kernel path under contention.
- KV-cache churn: token cache miss rate spiked (we're seeing 12–18% increase in cold-start misses) which magnifies decode overhead and increases CPU/GPU scheduling contention on the dedicated pool.
- End result: per-request latency up, effective throughput down, small increase in internal timeouts -> 5xx surface.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered):
1) Roll back PayLynx's traffic to v2.3 (fp16) on their dedicated pool — targeted rollback to their tenant. This is the fastest path to restore SLOs.
2) If rollback isn't possible quickly, disable int8 kernel selection for PayLynx and force fp16 execution.
3) Throttle batching to a lower max-batch-size for the affected route to avoid bursty tail latency.

I'm initiating a targeted rollback now and pushing a runbook note to the incident playbook. I'll attach the rollback-playbook and post a short run command in the ticket.

-- Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer

Jared — quick update and exec summary for your leadership:

Status (14:05 UTC):
- We initiated a targeted rollback of PayLynx traffic from v2.4 (int8) -> v2.3 (fp16) at 13:42 UTC.
- Telemetry shows p95 improving and error-rate trending down; Grafana shows recovery to ~260ms p95 and error-rate returning toward baseline.
- Root cause: runtime int8 kernel path + increased KV cache churn under PayLynx traffic pattern produced decode-side latency amplification. We're treating this as a release/regression issue.

Action items / next steps:
1) We will keep PayLynx on v2.3 for 48 hours while Rishi and infra run a focused repro and add mitigations (improved kernel fallbacks, more conservative int8 ramping controls).
2) We will run a postmortem and share a summary and timeline with you and your execs by end of day tomorrow.
3) Marissa will schedule a short follow-up between our technical leads and PayLynx SREs to align on a safe redeploy plan.

I have looped in Vivek (CTO) for visibility — we will escalate to a broader exec bridge if recovery stalls. Please confirm when your critical flows look healthy on your side.

Thanks for the quick signal and patience — we'll keep you posted every 30 minutes until stabilized.

Best,
